First-reader issue 1 (05-1 and 05-4 balloons cover Ananya's face): not confirmed. In 05-1 the art puts her face and hair edge at about x319-325, and the balloon starts at x354. Her raised hand (y244+) is below the balloon bottom (y178). In 05-4 her face ends at about x359-373 and the balloon starts at x404. The cut-off name labels are placeholder artifacts. One minor lettering check: the 05-4 balloon bottom (y1270) may just touch the top of her raised fingertips (about y1263, x437-513).

First-reader issue 2 (05-4 speaker ambiguity): the tail points left. In the art Ravi is nodding with motion lines and his mouth closed, and the line ('your concerns') is clearly the doctor's. Not a real problem.

First-reader issue 3 (05-2 balloon on the listener's side): top-left is the natural left-to-right entry point. In the art Ravi's mouth is open and Ananya is only the back of a head. The balloon (y568-673) grazes the top of her hair (about y646+), not a face. Acceptable.

First-reader issue 4 (05-3 caption on the border): cosmetic. In the art the caption bottom (y690) grazes the top of Ananya's hair (about y673) and the foreground back of Ravi's head. Her eyes are at about y754, so no face is covered.

First-reader issues 5 and 6 (thin consultation, 'Technology' has no referent): the lines are fixed by the source. The revision now places QR, TV and tablet technology on pages 3-4 right before this page, and the 05-3 art shows the closed laptop pushed aside. 'Technology' now has a referent, and the human-conversation contrast is stronger.

readingReview.comparison: My order agrees with the first reader's, with no skips. Their face-cover and speaker concerns come from the placeholder labels and are not borne out by the accepted art. The narrative-thinness point is source-dictated and is mitigated by the new pages 3-4.

Screen direction stays Ananya-left, Ravi-right through all four panels, including the over-the-shoulder reverse shots in 05-2 and 05-3.
